company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted that comp linearity improved through the quarter, which is providing some relief and lifting shares.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote at the Meta Connect conference Wednesday night at 7pm ET. Shopify announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, a meaningful distribution win as Amazon has blocked Muse from its own platform. Investor expectations are building bullishly into the event, and the stock is outperforming on the day.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases directly on its e-commerce platform, positioning Shopify as a key partner in the agentic commerce ecosystem. This contrasts with Amazon's decision to block Muse, potentially giving Shopify a competitive edge in agentic checkout adoption.

MillerKnoll reported solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and critically the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind, EPS was 42 cents, still well above consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales guidance trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged. The stock is an earnings-linked outperformer today.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margin weakness of 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% more than offset slightly better-than-expected revenue of $2.311 billion. Management explicitly cited a difficult macro landscape, raising concerns about the consumer discretionary environment. The stock is an earnings-linked underperformer.

Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp shares were hit following new Medicare payment rates from CMS for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. Both stocks are underperforming meaningfully on the day as investors reprice the earnings impact of the rate cuts.

Lab Corp is selling off alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that came in more negative than expected. The sector reprice is broader than just one name, reflecting a systemic headwind for lab testing companies.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the study. This is a strong clinical readout that keeps Viking competitive in the increasingly crowded but high-growth obesity drug space.

Alibaba unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip and hinted at plans to train a model with up to 10 trillion parameters, while management outlined plans to operate more than 20 gigawatts of data center capacity by 2032. The announcement positions Alibaba as a serious domestic AI infrastructure competitor and is a positive catalyst for the stock.

A WWD article published Tuesday speculates that Capri Holdings, the parent of Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo, may be exploring a sale. No deal has been confirmed, but the report is generating M&A speculation around the stock.

tts_summary:
Here's your midday update for Tuesday September 22nd.

Markets are mixed and largely directionless at this hour. The S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, but the Dow is down 43 basis points and the equal-weight S&P is slightly negative. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is just below a hundred dollars a barrel, off modestly on hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough with Iran — Tehran has apparently offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia is signaling its East-West Pipeline may be coming partially back online, which is also easing some of the oil risk premium.

The real story right now is that investors are positioning ahead of a massive AI catalyst cluster. Zuckerberg's keynote at the Meta Connect conference is tomorrow night. OpenAI's DevDay is September 29th. And Micron reports earnings on September 30th. Meta is one of the standout performers today — Muse, their personal AI agent, is seeing surging downloads, and Shopify just announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform, a big win given that Amazon blocked it. Alibaba is also in focus after unveiling what it called China's most powerful AI chip and hinting at a model with up to ten trillion parameters.

On earnings, AutoZone beat on the bottom line — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street at fifty-four — but the quality was poor. The upside was driven by tariff refunds and a non-cash accounting benefit, while domestic comps missed at plus one-point-six percent versus the Street's plus three-point-one. Management said linearity improved through the quarter, which is helping the stock. MillerKnoll was a cleaner beat — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six cents expected, and even stripping out the tariff refund tailwind, they still beat. Thor Industries missed — seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected — with gross margins down 230 basis points year-over-year, and management was cautious on the macro backdrop.

Viking Therapeutics is getting attention after reporting positive trial data on its GLP-1 drug showing 22 percent weight loss. That's a strong number in the obesity space.

On the downside, financials are broadly under pressure — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers are all in the red. Lab testing names Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp got hit hard after CMS released new Medicare lab service rates that were worse than expected. And Capri Holdings is in the news on speculation the company may be exploring a sale.

The directional read today is neutral to cautiously constructive. The indices aren't doing much, but the AI setup into next week is substantial. Watch the Meta keynote tomorrow night — that's the near-term catalyst that could set the tone for the whole tech complex into month-end. After the close today, KB Home and one other name report earnings. Stay nimble.
